model.description: A whole economy on a single balance sheet — households, firms, banks and a consolidated government (Treasury + central bank) — built to show how the pieces connect. Government spending credits household deposits and creates money (GovDep goes negative); taxes destroy it; banks create money by lending (private debt); and a bond market lets the public swap money for interest-bearing government bonds. It is stock-flow consistent by construction, so every dollar is someone's asset and someone's liability, and net_worth_check stays ~0. Watch private wealth grow by exactly the government's deficit — the sectoral balances identity — and note that selling bonds only swaps money for bonds; it never 'funds' the spending, which already happened. This is the plumbing behind money creation, the govt-is-not-a-household point, and endogenous private debt.
